harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Established an AIDE-based file-integrity baseline for /etc on node1 (RHEL 9.8): installed aide, scoped /etc/aide.conf to /etc (disabled non-etc top-level trees /boot,/bin,/sbin,/lib,/lib64,/opt,/usr,/root), and strengthened the catch-all /etc rule from PERMS to NORMAL to add content hashing, since the stock PERMS-only rule silently missed content-only edits to files without an explicit rule (proven via an /etc/motd test). Initialized the AIDE database (1131 entries), verified a clean check, verified detection of a deliberate content change, then reverted the test change and re-verified clean. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured boot_id and AIDE db checksum pre-restart, issued a detached systemctl reboot so the ack returned before disconnect, polled until node1 was reachable again, confirmed boot_id changed (bf4e9cbb-84f9-45f0-9b81-6602b98cea07 -> 4e4bd6a3-e34e-42dd-8fc8-71d0a915e4ad), and confirmed the AIDE config, database checksum, and a fresh aide --check all show the baseline intact and clean post-restart.
actions_performed: Installed aide package on node1 via dnf
Backed up /etc/aide.conf to /etc/aide.conf.orig
Edited /etc/aide.conf to exclude non-/etc top-level paths (/boot,/bin,/sbin,/lib,/lib64,/opt,/usr,/root) to scope the baseline to /etc
Changed the /etc catch-all rule from PERMS to NORMAL to enable content hashing for all /etc files not otherwise explicitly matched
Ran aide --init and activated the resulting database as /var/lib/aide/aide.db.gz
Ran aide --check to confirm a clean baseline (no differences, 1131 entries)
Appended text to /etc/motd and re-ran aide --check to prove the baseline detects and reports the change (Changed entry with SHA512/SHA3-256 diff)
Reverted /etc/motd to its original empty state and confirmed aide --check returns clean again
Captured pre-restart boot_id and AIDE db sha256sum on node1
Issued a detached systemctl reboot on node1 so the acknowledgement returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until command execution was available again
Confirmed boot_id changed post-restart, proving an actual reboot occurred
Verified AIDE config (/etc catch-all rule), database checksum, and a fresh aide --check all matched pre-restart state, confirming the baseline persisted and recovery was clean

evidence.requirement: AIDE installed and /etc integrity baseline initialized on node1
evidence.summary: Confirmed RHEL 9.8, aide absent, then installed aide and ran aide --init producing a 1131-entry database, activated as aide.db.gz

evidence.requirement: Baseline config scoped and strengthened for /etc content tracking
evidence.summary: Reviewed default aide.conf, excluded non-/etc trees, and upgraded the /etc catch-all from PERMS to NORMAL for content hashing

evidence.requirement: Baseline is clean and functional (no false positives)
evidence.summary: Re-initialized database under final config; aide --check repeatedly reports NO differences, 1131 entries

evidence.requirement: Baseline detects and reports later changes to /etc files (core task requirement)
evidence.summary: Deliberate edit to /etc/motd was reported by aide --check as a Changed entry with file size and hash diffs, proving detection works

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline captured on node1
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id bf4e9cbb-84f9-45f0-9b81-6602b98cea07, AIDE db sha256sum, and a clean aide --check immediately before reboot
Detached/backgrounded systemctl reboot command returned 'reboot scheduled' successfully before the node dropped

evidence.requirement: Node1 boot identity proven changed after restart
evidence.summary: Connection failures during reboot window followed by successful reconnection showing new boot_id 4e4bd6a3-e34e-42dd-8fc8-71d0a915e4ad, differing from pre-restart value

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of integrity baseline and required state on node1
evidence.summary: Post-reboot: uptime reflects new boot, AIDE db checksum unchanged, /etc catch-all NORMAL rule intact, and aide --check reports clean with 1131 entries, confirming full recovery
